summary.text: 33y male, nonsmoking and systemically healthy, with ASA class given as ASA I. The table records RT3 recession at mandibular two centrals with facial recession of 5 mm at baseline, and Jemt's papilla index of 0 before treatment. Papilla loss in the esthetic zone is stated for the five individuals.

Before surgery the patient completed initial periodontal therapy and received detailed oral hygiene instructions, and informed consent was obtained. The patient underwent the inverted T-shape connective tissue graft procedure for interdental papilla reconstruction at the treated site listed in the table.

The table lists root coverage achieved as Partial (2–3 mm) and Jemt's papilla index of 2 after treatment, with follow-up of 6 m. Esthetic outcomes were acceptable and morbidity was minimal across all patients.

The Figure 7 caption describes clinical and radiographic examinations showing RT3 gingival recession between teeth #24 and #25 and 3 weeks of follow-up of the donor and recipient sites. The Figure 4 caption, stated to be the same patient, documents the palatal harvest: guide placement, incisions around the guide, removal of the T-shaped free gingival graft, and collagen tape over the harvest site.

summary.text: 66y female, nonsmoking and systemically healthy, with ASA class given as ASA I. The table records RT2 recession at maxillary two centrals with facial recession of 3 mm at baseline, and Jemt's papilla index of 0 before treatment. Papilla loss in the esthetic zone is stated for the five individuals.

Before surgery the patient completed initial periodontal therapy and received detailed oral hygiene instructions, and informed consent was obtained. The patient underwent the inverted T-shape connective tissue graft procedure for interdental papilla reconstruction at the treated site listed in the table.

The table lists root coverage achieved as Full coverage and Jemt's papilla index of 2 after treatment, with follow-up of 6 m. Esthetic outcomes were acceptable and morbidity was minimal across all patients.

The Figure 1 caption, linked to this patient only by matching attributes, describes clinical and radiographic examination showing RT2 gingival recession at teeth #8 and #9, with significant gingival tissue loss and root exposure before surgery. Surgery included tunneling of the mesio-buccal sulcus, a vertical incision apical to the defect, IT-CTG placement and an additional CTG at the #6 site, with sutures securing the grafts. At six months the caption reports successful graft integration, complete coverage of the defect and maintained gingival health.

caption_evidence.quote: A nonsmoking, systemically healthy 66‐year‐old female. Clinical and radiographic examination revealed recession type 2 (RT2) gingival recession in her anterior maxilla, specifically at the sites of teeth #8 and #9. (a) Pre‐surgical clinical photo showing the recession defect at the facial aspect of teeth #8 and #9, with significant gingival tissue loss and root exposure. (b) Tunneling of the mesio‐buccal sulcus using a microsurgical tunneling instrument to create a donor site for the connective tissue graft (CTG) while preserving the vascular supply to the gingival tissue. (c) Vertical incision made apical to the defect site to facilitate graft placement and provide access for tissue mobilization. (d) Placement of an in situ connective tissue graft (IT‐CTG) at the defect site involving teeth #8 and #9, along with additional placement of a CTG at the #6 site to enhance the overall esthetic and functional outcome. (e) Immediately post‐surgery, showing the grafts in place with sutures securing the tissue, providing tension‐free closure. (f) Six‐month follow‐up showing successful graft integration, with complete coverage of the recession defect and maintained gingival health at the treated sites.

caption_evidence.quote: Surgical tunneling kit used for the inverted T‐shape connective tissue graft (IT‐CTG) procedure. The kit includes three specifically designed microsurgical instruments that facilitate precise access to the interdental papilla through the vestibule. These instruments enable atraumatic tunneling and optimal placement of the graft in challenging interproximal areas (Nexton, Sialkot—Pakistan).

caption_evidence.quote: (a) Pre‐surgical clinical photo showing an inverted T‐shaped guide made from a sterile aluminum sheet. The guide is designed to outline the graft harvest site for precision and to ensure proper graft dimensions. Measurements of the T‐shaped guide illustrate the precise dimensions of the harvest area to ensure consistency and optimal graft size. (b) Photo showing the guide placed at the desired harvest site on the palate, ensuring the graft is harvested from the correct location for sufficient tissue. (c) Initial incision lines made around the guide, preparing for the removal of the free gingival graft (FGG). (d) Removal of the T‐shaped free gingival graft (FGG), prior to extra‐oral de‐epithelialization. The graft is carefully lifted to preserve its integrity and minimize trauma to the surrounding tissue. (e) Harvest site following the removal of the FGG, showing the exposed donor tissue area that will heal after the graft is removed. (f) Immediate post‐surgery photo showing collagen tape placed over the harvest site to achieve hemostasis and promote early healing.
